items.title: Show HN: AgentRun: DSL to turn agents into workflows
items.excerpt:
Hi HN, I just open sourced the DSL that our harness in grep.ai uses to turn repeatable parts of agent work into workflows. You can combine tool calls, code, Jev-powered system one decisions for things like routing and screening evidence, and agents when a step needs more investigation. Our harness uses the traces and retro notes agents leave behind when doing a job to figure out which parts can become a workflow. The idea is to make the work easier to understand and avoid paying for a full agent loop where one isn’t needed.
For example, a research workflow can split a question into subquestion
items.summary: AgentRun is a DSL that converts repeatable agent work into workflows by combining tool calls, code, typed decisions, and agents; traces from agent jobs identify which parts can become workflows to reduce unnecessary agent loop costs.
items.usefulness: If building Python document analysis tools, could structure multi-step agent tasks (research, routing, evidence screening) into reusable workflows to lower inference costs on repetitive patterns.
items.to_verify: Whether AgentRun actually reduces costs versus full agent loops on real document analysis tasks, and what 'Jev-powered system one decisions' concretely implements.
